model_interpretation.claim: Packing short H rows into each CTA should reduce CTA overhead and inactive threads in the separate forward and input-gradient passes. The mapping uses row_width=min(L,256) and packs floor(256/row_width) rows per CTA; for L=48, this assigns five rows to a 240-thread CTA instead of launching one 256-thread CTA per row. Rows of length at least 256 retain the existing one-row, 256-thread mapping. The baseline is correct at 35.464 ms mean for the full call, but it does not isolate these kernels; any benefit remains unmeasured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Map each forward and input-gradient CTA across multiple H rows when L is below 256: block.x is L and block.y is floor(256/L), with a bounds guard for incomplete H groups.","Keep 256-wide x tiles and one row per CTA for L >= 256, preserving the existing per-row output mapping for longer rows.","Retain the separate FP32 forward and input-gradient passes, their bounds-safe zero padding and complete writes; leave the weight-gradient kernel unchanged."]}

model_interpretation.claim: A CTA per (h,j) can parallelize the weight-gradient accumulation over both batch and time, replacing the current serial B*L traversal for each output with per-thread FP32 accumulators and a shared-memory CTA reduction. The launch adapts its 2D block shape to B and L while capping the block at 256 threads. This may improve large reductions but add CTA and reduction overhead for small workloads; complete-call timing is needed to judge it.

items.subject: Combiner le mapping T1 et la réduction gk T3
items.objective: Partir du programme T3, le plus rapide mesuré, et y intégrer le mapping séparé des kernels forward et input-gradient de T1. Conserver la réduction gk de T3. Mesurer le programme complet et vérifier la correction; ne pas présumer que les gains s’additionnent.
